content.intro: This lesson focuses on advantages and limitations and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Advantages and Limitations matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Structured data lets different tools exchange values and relationships without agreeing on a programming language. JSON emphasizes strict, compact syntax; YAML prioritizes human-readable layout and adds features such as comments and multiple documents.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Readability. Portability. Maintainability. Data type representation. Strictness versus flexibility. Parser and implementation differences.; Compatibility and interoperability limitations.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect the example and compare it against the lesson concepts. This code block is static-validation: CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary data parsers or commands in the standard browser preview.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the starting fixture before each test. Change one field, indentation level, parser option, or schema constraint at a time, then compare the result with the prediction.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Keep the example small, name the intended data types, and verify it with both a valid case and an invalid or boundary case. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second synthetic fixture for “Readability. Portability. Maintainability. Data type representation. Strictness versus flexibility. Parser and implementation differences.”. Predict the parsed types/result, change one relevant detail, and record whether the target tool behaved as expected. Include one invalid or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
